effect_estimate.comment: Logged monthly income is also positively associated with logged consumption (Est. = 0.19, SE = 0.05, p < .001) and affordability (Est. = 3.03, SE = 0.45, OR = 20.68, p < .001).
effect_estimate.value: In multivariable regressions (N = 396), having an own household Baguio Water District (BWD) metered connection (vs. no connection) is positively associated with logged water consumption (Est. = 0.24, SE = 0.07, p < .01; +27.2% liters/capita/day), perceived cleanliness PCA score (Est. = 0.35, SE = 0.13, p < .01), extreme ease of access (Est. = 0.77, SE = 0.26, OR = 2.16, p < .01), and water affordability [spending <=10% of income] (Est. = 1.01, SE = 0.42, OR = 2.76, p < .05). Having a shared/other BWD connection (vs. none) is associated with lower consumption (Est. = -0.23, SE = 0.07, p < .001; -20.8%) and higher affordability (Est. = 1.00, SE = 0.44, OR = 2.71, p < .05). Homeownership has no statistically significant association with consumption (Est. = 0.09, SE = 0.07), cleanliness (Est. = 0.20, SE = 0.12), ease (Est. = -0.07, SE = 0.23, OR = 0.94), or affordability (Est. = -0.26, SE = 0.46, OR = 0.77). Qualitative interviews (n = 18) show that high upfront connection costs (₱6,000 BWD fee plus ₱4,000–₱8,000 piping installation = ₱10,000–₱14,000), discretionary case-by-case installment plans (₱3,000 initial + ₱3,000 over 3 months) with low public awareness, and burdensome/informal application processing exclude low-income households from formal connections.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 13-15 (Table 2 and Regression Results); PDF pp. 18-19 (Qualitative Findings: Household BWD connections)

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 under the design ceiling for cross-sectional mixed-methods studies (MMAT). sample_size.comment: From a canvassed frame of 1,793 housing units in Pinget, 454 were randomly selected (25% per stratum), 38 excluded for vacancy/duplication, and 396 of 416 eligible participated (95.2%). 18 survey respondents (15 women, 3 men) completed purposive in-depth interviews.
